svg.title: Chisum: electrical one-line diagram, JS8-851 revision 0
svg.text: JS8-851 · her supply, the boards that feed the navigation bridge, and every way on the bridge's five boards. Read with the proof of supply (ferry/yard/calc/JS8-851-proof-of-supply.md) and the cable schedule (JS8-856).
F1 from LB: 25 A, 2 × 6 mm², 33.5 m, 1.7 %
Bridge deck lighting, corridor and after platform
F1 from TSB: 10 A, 2 × 2.5 mm², 29.5 m, 0.6
F2 from LB: 10 A, 2 × 4 mm², 44.0 m, 0.6 %
24 V DC panel, navigation and control
F1 from DCB: 40 A, 2 × 35 mm², 24.5 m, 3.3 %
6 Navigation data: distributor, network switch, co…
11 Alarm panel, watch alarm, door and ramp panel
12 Heading and bearing repeaters, rudder angle ind…
14 Public address and general alarm, battery supply
15 Night and transitional lighting, binnacle light
circuits that leave a board elsewhere direct, each on a breaker of its own there
joined; lines that cross without a dot are not

A breaker is at least 1.25 times the full-load current; a cable is rated for its breaker; no cable loses more than 5 % of the voltage, and no consumer more than 6 % in all from the switchboard (10 % on a battery supply). A cable's length is the way it is laid along, and a tenth more.
Each way reads: its number and name; then the breaker, the cable (two cores and an earth), the connected load, the length to its farthest consumer and the voltage lost from the switchboard to it.

Infeeds of one voltage are joined before they are transformed. The emergency switchboard: A 440 V board, fed from the main board's 440 V section through the bus-tie while there is main power, and from the emergency generator within 45 s of losing it; its 230 V section, which feeds the bridge, is behind the 5 kVA emergency lighting transformer.

The transitional section: A section of the emergency switchboard that is never dead: fed from the board while it is alive, and without a break from the general service battery through a 1 kVA inverter (24 V DC to 230 V) when it is not. It feeds the navigation light panel.
The 690 V and 440 V systems are three-wire and insulated; 230 V and 24 V are two-wire, both poles insulated and both switched, which is why every breaker drawn opens both.

The sheet shows the register as it stands: the navigation bridge and what feeds it. Her machinery, lighting, galley and ramps are not registered yet and are not drawn. Sizes of the generators and transformers are the register's, not calculated here (the load balance of the whole ship is to do: JS8-852).

Made by ferry/yard/drawings/electrical_drawing.py from ferry/data/systems.json (the component register). The standards a board is built to are named on the board sheets, JS8-864, and are recalled there, not read.
